subject: Provisional credit authorization and VAT scheduling for March overage
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@clearcarehealth.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.com
Cc: accounts-payable@clearcarehealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected March usage spike — request for provisional credit and VAT guidance

Hi Michael,

We noticed a very large spike in token consumption on our March 1st runs (attached usage_report_Mar2027.csv). This appears to be due to an integration job that backfilled two days of events. Our finance team is asking whether Redwood can provisionally apply a credit to offset ~EUR 18,400 of the overage while we complete our post-mortem.

Two things we need: 1) confirmation that Redwood will hold the credit in escrow or apply as a goodwill credit pending audit, and 2) instructions on what VAT documentation you need from us so the credit can be processed correctly for EU reporting. We can upload the VAT certificate and vendor forms immediately.

Can you let us know the quickest path? We are on a close month-end and need to reconcile this with our AR.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Finance Lead — ClearCare Health
liam.oconnor@clearcarehealth.com

Attachments: usage_report_Mar2027.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: michael_grant@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@clearcarehealth.com>, accounts-payable@clearcarehealth.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected March usage spike — request for provisional credit and VAT guidance

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the usage report. Sorry to hear about the backfill. We can absolutely help smooth this for month-end. Proposed approach: 

- Redwood can issue a provisional "goodwill" credit for the disputed amount (EUR 18,400) and either hold it as an internal credit balance on your account or place it in a short-term escrow pending the outcome of your internal post-mortem and our audit.
- To process the credit and handle VAT correctly, we need ClearCare's VAT certificate and the legal billing entity name. For EU VAT reclaim/crediting we generally need: VAT registration certificate (PDF), company name on invoice, and confirmation of billing country.
- We will generate a provisional credit note (provisional_credit_agreement.pdf) and mark it as pending. If the audit shows the charge was valid, we will discuss a two-way settlement; if the overage is confirmed, the credit will be finalized and applied to your next invoice.

Next steps: Liam, can you upload the VAT certificate (vat_certificate_clearcare.pdf) and confirm the exact billing entity? Ben, Marcus — can you review and approve the provisional credit hold for EUR 18,400 so I can route this to Finance (Naomi) for processing? Ben, if we apply this as a temporary account credit, what operational flags do we need? Marcus, any tax-specific guidance for EU treatments?

I can sign the provisional agreement once we have the docs.

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Sales Lead — Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: provisional_credit_agreement.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: michael_grant@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional credit authorization and VAT scheduling for March overage

On Thu, Mar 2, 2027 at 10:05 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben, Marcus — can you review and approve the provisional credit hold for EUR 18,400 so I can route this to Finance (Naomi) for processing?

Michael / Marcus — I approve placing a provisional credit hold for the requested amount and recommend hold-as-credit on the account for now (faster reconciliation for AR). Naomi, can you create a pending credit memo and mark the transaction as "provisional: customer dispute" in the ledger? Also list the VAT evidence requirement as a dependency before finalization.

Marcus — for EU VAT, ensure we don't net the VAT unless ClearCare supplies a valid certificate matching the billing entity. If they do, we can reduce the VAT portion on the credit note; otherwise issue the credit inclusive of VAT and adjust later.

Naomi — please route the provisional_credit_agreement.pdf to Legal for a quick sign-off, then apply the conditional credit. Put a 45-day expiry on the provisional hold.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: (none)

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@clearcarehealth.com>, michael_grant@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional credit authorization and VAT scheduling for March overage

Hi Liam — thanks for sending the VAT certificate (received at 09:12 today). We have: 

- Created a pending credit memo for EUR 18,400 and applied it as an account credit (status: provisional).
- Uploaded the supporting docs to the finance ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-7593.
- VAT certificate verified against the billing entity and country — we will issue the final credit note net of VAT once the internal audit confirms the backfill root cause.
- The provisional credit will expire in 45 days unless you request an extension. If the audit adjusts the amount, we will reissue a corrected credit note and notify you.

Please confirm you received the provisional_credit_agreement.pdf with the hold terms and whether you prefer the credit applied to next invoice or refunded as payment. If refund is preferred, we will start the refund flow and include VAT adjustments in the remittance.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Revenue Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: vat_certificate_clearcare.pdf (PDF, 24KB)
